**The per-machine adapter, and the answer carried back**

## Context

Sessions Mustur starts, can type into and can stop, and the delivery of an answered decision into the session that raised it. It does not supervise them; that moved to 4b.

## Discharges

Part of MUS-M-0006 (4a): the adapter starts a long-lived session per project inside tmux, and an answered decision is delivered back into the session that raised it.

## Done means

mustur session start runs a configured CLI in a named tmux session, one per project, refusing a second.
It refuses a --dir that is not a directory, because tmux silently falls back to $HOME and a session reported as running in a checkout would not be.
It reports a command that exited immediately rather than calling it started, watching for a short window because tmux does not reap synchronously.
mustur session list and stop act only on sessions this adapter started, established by a tmux user option it sets rather than by the session's name.
No tmux server is reported as no sessions rather than as a failure, and a real tmux failure is still a failure.
Answering a question that names a session with --in types the answer into it, prefixed with the question identifier and the fact that the owner answered.
An answer whose session is gone, or whose delivery fails or times out, is still recorded, carrying the reason.
An answer is not lost when the client disconnects mid-delivery.

## Risks

Mustur can put words into an agent's input, and at the far end that is indistinguishable from the owner typing. The limits are the ownership option, the self-describing text, and the answer path being the only caller — all enforced in code, none enforced by anything outside this repository.
tmux is the only record of what is running, so a tmux server death loses every session and everything known about them. That is the accepted cost of not mirroring.
A session is started with whatever --cmd is passed; nothing validates that the command is an agent CLI rather than anything else on the machine.
Nothing supervises a session after it settles. A CLI that crashes a second after starting is reported as started, and nothing notices it die. Supervision is 4b's.
The ownership option is not a security boundary: anyone who can run tmux as this user can set it. It distinguishes Mustur's sessions from a person's, not from an adversary's.
